text:
Philadelphia played the better game and lost it. The Flyers carried 3.4 expected goals to Ottawa's 2.27, and in a simulated replay of every shot they win 70 percent of the time. What they could not do was get anything past Linus Ullmark, who stopped 28 of 29 shots and saved 2.4 goals more than the chances against him deserved.

The second period was where the gap opened. PHI outchanced OTT 1.97 to 0.68 in expected goals, and Matvei Michkov tied it at 1-1 with a backhand on the power play at 7:46, an 85 percent chance by the numbers. Sean Couturier had the best look that didn't go in, a 28 percent chance that Ullmark turned away. Nick Cousins had given OTT the early lead at 10:14 of the first with a tip-in, an 11 percent chance.

The winner came at 13:01 of the third, and it was the least likely goal of the night. Carter Yakemchuk beat Joseph Woll with a slap shot on the power play, a 6 percent chance, assisted by Claude Giroux and Shane Pinto. OTT blocked 20 shots to PHI's 11, which helped hold off a team that attempted 64 shots to 50. Yakemchuk and Ullmark were named second and third stars behind T. Chabot.
